title: Kunal Kemmu's 'Vibe' Jumps on Day 2, Beats 'Madgaon Express' Two-Day Total
excerpt: The spy comedy earned an estimated ₹2.5–2.8 crore net on Saturday, pushing its two-day total past Kunal Kemmu's directorial debut and setting up a projected ₹7.5–8 crore opening weekend.
body:
• Kunal Kemmu's spy comedy Vibe collected an estimated ₹2.5–2.8 crore net on Saturday, taking its two-day domestic total to roughly ₹4.2–5.05 crore, depending on the tracker.
  • That two-day figure has already crossed the two-day total of Kemmu's directorial debut Madgaon Express (₹4.35 crore), per trade reports.
  • The film opened on September 18 opposite Meghna Gulzar's Daayra and is currently leading the weekend, with trade projections of a ₹7.5–8 crore opening weekend.
  • Co-starring Preity Zinta, Sparsh Shrivastava and Vanshika Dhir, Vibe is produced by Drongo Films in association with Amazon MGM Studios.

A Saturday Surge

Kunal Kemmu's Vibe found its footing on its second day. The spy action-comedy, which opened on Friday, September 18, to a modest start, posted a healthy jump on Saturday — collecting between ₹2.5 crore and ₹2.8 crore net in India, according to trade trackers including Sacnilk. With around 21% overall occupancy across 2,979 shows and night shows peaking near 33%, the film's two-day domestic net now stands between ₹4.2 crore and ₹5.05 crore, the range reflecting differences between trackers.

The more telling number is comparative. Per trade reports, Vibe's two-day total has already crossed the two-day domestic earnings of Kemmu's 2024 directorial debut, Madgaon Express, which managed ₹4.35 crore across its first two days (₹1.63 crore on day one, ₹2.72 crore on day two). Koimoi's trade desk, which first flagged the milestone, put Vibe's day-two figure at ₹2.8 crore and its two-day total at ₹5.05 crore, projecting an opening weekend approaching ₹8 crore. Pinkvilla, using slightly more conservative estimates, sees the film aiming for around ₹7.5 crore for the weekend.

Context & Background

Vibe is Kemmu's second outing as a director, following Madgaon Express, the 2024 comedy that grew from a modest theatrical run into a wider audience on streaming. The new film — described variously as a spy comedy and a heist comedy — stars Kemmu himself alongside Preity Zinta, Sparsh Shrivastava and Vanshika Dhir, and is produced by Kemmu and Chirag Nihalani under the Drongo Films banner in association with Amazon MGM Studios.

The premise puts two untrained, ordinary people inside a high-stakes espionage mission — ordinary characters colliding with the world of spies. Speaking to PTI, Kemmu said the idea predates his directing career entirely, and explained the film's references to popular fictional spies such as Pathaan and Tiger as a function of character psychology: an untrained person dropped into a spy mission would naturally reach for the pop-culture figures they know.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=meknZizkusk

"I've had this story with me even before I became a director. I've narrated this to friends. I didn't write it then because I didn't know whether it would be made or not."

— Kunal Kemmu, actor-director, to PTI

The weekend is a crowded one. Vibe is running directly against Meghna Gulzar's crime thriller Daayra, starring Kareena Kapoor Khan and Prithviraj Sukumaran — a clash of two very different Hindi films on the same Friday. Early trade data gives Vibe the edge: Daayra was reported at roughly ₹1.6 crore net on day two with about 17% occupancy across 2,061 shows, trailing Vibe on both collections and footfall.

Impact & Analysis

For Kemmu, the day-two trajectory matters more than the absolute numbers. Madgaon Express proved he could direct a profitable comedy; Vibe's Saturday growth — a jump of roughly 47–65% over Friday, depending on the tracker — suggests word of mouth is doing its job after mixed-to-positive reviews. The audience response has singled out the Kemmu–Sparsh Shrivastava dynamic, Zinta's action-heavy turn, and Dhir's performance, according to trade coverage.

The ₹7.5–8 crore weekend projection is modest by star-vehicle standards but meaningful in context: it would put Vibe firmly ahead of Kemmu's debut and establish him as a repeatable comedy director rather than a one-film wonder. The Amazon MGM Studios association also signals the studio's continued bet on mid-budget Hindi comedies with streaming afterlives — Madgaon Express found its largest audience after theatres, and Vibe is structured for the same second act.

Diaspora Angle

For the diaspora, Vibe carries two hooks. The first is Preity Zinta, whose return to a substantial Hindi-film role will draw NRI audiences who grew up on her 2000s stardom. The second is the film's positioning: a light spy comedy built on pop-culture references to Pathaan and Tiger travels well, since diaspora viewers are often more fluent in Bollywood's shared mythology than in any single film's plot. If Vibe follows the Madgaon Express playbook — modest theatricals, long streaming tail — its real diaspora moment will come when it lands on Prime Video.

What's Next

Sunday will decide the story. A sustained hold would lock in the ₹7.5–8 crore weekend and set Vibe up for a profitable first week, especially with no major Hindi release crowding the following Friday. A sharp Sunday drop, on the other hand, would leave it dependent on the streaming afterlife its predecessor enjoyed. Either way, Kemmu has already cleared the bar that mattered most: his second film is outperforming his first.
